title: Numbers, time and dates
summary: Count from 0 to 100 (soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix), tell the time, and say the days, months and dates.
focus: Numbers to 100, telling the time and giving dates
content:
## Numbers from 0 to 100

- 0–10: **zéro, un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix**
- 11–20: **onze, douze, treize, quatorze, quinze, seize, dix-sept, dix-huit, dix-neuf, vingt**
- tens: **trente** (30), **quarante** (40), **cinquante** (50), **soixante** (60)
- 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 take **et un** (**vingt et un**), and the others take a hyphen (**vingt-deux, trente-cinq**)

From 70, French counts in twenties:

- **soixante-dix** (60 + 10 = 70), **soixante et onze** (71), **soixante-quinze** (75)
- **quatre-vingts** (4 × 20 = 80). The s goes when a number follows: **quatre-vingt-un** (81, no **et**)
- **quatre-vingt-dix** (90), **quatre-vingt-dix-neuf** (99), **cent** (100)

To ask or give your age: **Quel âge as-tu ?** **J'ai trente-cinq ans.**

## Telling the time

**Quelle heure est-il ?** **Il est trois heures.** Always say **heure(s)**, as in **il est une heure**, **il est deux heures**.

- **et quart** (quarter past): **huit heures et quart** (8:15)
- **et demie** (half past): **huit heures et demie** (8:30)
- **moins le quart** (quarter to): **neuf heures moins le quart** (8:45)
- minutes: **neuf heures dix** (9:10), **neuf heures moins dix** (8:50)
- **midi** (noon), **minuit** (midnight)

Timetables, shops and the radio use the **24-hour clock**, written **17h30**: **Le train part à dix-sept heures trente.** With it you just say the minutes (**quinze heures quarante-cinq**), never *et quart*. At a time is **à**: **à huit heures**.

## Days, months and dates

Days and months are written in **lower case**.

- days: **lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche**. **Lundi** means this Monday, and **le lundi** means on Mondays.
- months: **janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre**. In May is **en mai**.

A date is **le** + number + month: **le trois juin** (June 3rd), **le quatorze juillet**. Only the first day is different: **le premier mai** (May 1st). To ask the date, say **On est le combien ?** **On est le vingt mars.**

concept.title: Septante and nonante
concept.markdown: In Belgium and Switzerland, 70 is **septante** and 90 **nonante**; parts of Switzerland also say **huitante** for 80. In France you will only hear **soixante-dix**, **quatre-vingts** and **quatre-vingt-dix**, and they are understood everywhere.

bites.title: Counting to 69
bites.rule: Tens: dix, vingt, trente, quarante, cinquante, soixante. 21, 31, 41, 51 and 61 take et un (vingt et un), and the rest take a hyphen (vingt-deux).

bites.title: 70 to 99
bites.rule: 70 = soixante-dix (60 + 10), 80 = quatre-vingts (4 × 20), 90 = quatre-vingt-dix. 80 drops its s before another number: quatre-vingt-un.

bites.title: Quelle heure est-il ?
bites.rule: Say il est + heures, then et quart (:15), et demie (:30) or moins le quart (:45). Timetables use the 24-hour clock: dix-sept heures trente.
bites.example: Il est neuf heures moins le quart.

bites.title: Dates
bites.rule: Le + number + month, all lower case: le trois juin. The first is le premier, as in le premier mai.

sorts.title: Which number?
sorts.why: Soixante + 10 to 19 gives 70–79; quatre-vingt + 0 to 9 gives 80–89; quatre-vingt + 10 to 19 gives 90–99.

sorts.title: After or before the hour?
sorts.why: Et and a plain number of minutes go after the hour, and moins counts down to it.

realm.content:
## Compter à Eldmark

At the Highgate market, gold talks. **La potion coûte soixante-quinze pièces d'or.** The guild meets **le premier mars à neuf heures et demie**, and the dungeon opens **à minuit**. Borin counts his loot: **quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix, cent !**

meadowbrook.content:
## Les heures à Meadowbrook

The rooster crows **à six heures moins le quart**. Rosa opens the seed shop **à neuf heures**, from **lundi** to **samedi**. Strawberries cost **quatre-vingts centimes**. The fishing contest is **le premier juillet**, and the harvest festival **le vingt-deux septembre**.

vocabulary.example_meaning: What time is it? Six o'clock, time to work!

rustwake.content:
## Le temps à Rustwake

Your **radio-montre** keeps Dôme time on the 24-hour clock. **Il est dix-sept heures quarante.** Marta's stall closes **à dix-neuf heures**. Filtered water costs **soixante-dix écrous**, a Saphir soda **quatre-vingt-quinze**. The ash storm comes **le premier août**.

vocabulary.example_meaning: What time is it? My wrist radio says noon.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Filtered water costs seventy nuts.

vocabulary.example: Le tonique coûte quatre-vingt-dix écrous.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The tonic costs ninety nuts.

vocabulary.example: Cent écrous pour un disque ? C'est cher !
vocabulary.example_meaning: A hundred nuts for a record? That's expensive!

vocabulary.example_meaning: August is the month of storms.
